goal: Unify priority notation across the SDD flow so that draft, spec.md, and spec.json all use the same enum: must, should, nice-to-have.
background: The prioritize-requirements guardrail instructs authors to specify their priority order without naming the enum that spec.json accepts. AI agents interpret this as P1/P2/P3 notation, which spec.json schema validation rejects. This mismatch caused schema validation failures (documented in spec 227 issue-log).

in: Change the prioritize-requirements guardrail body to explicitly name the spec.json priority enum values (must, should, nice-to-have).
out: Changing the spec.json schema priority enum.
Changing render, review, or retro logic.

constraints: The guardrail body is plain text evaluated by AI during gate checks. It must be concise and unambiguous.
Impact on existing features: gate-draft and gate-spec AI evaluation will see updated guardrail text. No impact on spec.json schema, spec render, review, or retro logic.
design_principles: Single source of truth: the spec.json schema defines the canonical priority values; the guardrail references them.

modules.text: src/presets/base/guardrail.json — contains the prioritize-requirements guardrail definition.

data_flow.text: guardrail.json → gate-draft/gate-spec AI evaluation → draft.md/spec.md authoring → spec.json validation.

decisions.text: Chose A+C (unify notation + update guardrail wording) over B (auto-normalize) and D (relax schema).

requirements.desc: When requirements exceed three items, the prioritize-requirements guardrail body shall instruct authors to assign each requirement a priority from the spec.json enum: must, should, or nice-to-have.
When the prioritize-requirements guardrail body is rendered for AI evaluation, it shall not reference or permit P1/P2/P3 notation as a valid priority format.

acceptance_criteria: npm test passes with no regressions.
The prioritize-requirements guardrail body in src/presets/base/guardrail.json contains the values must, should, nice-to-have.
The guardrail body does not reference P1/P2/P3 notation.

clarifications.q: Why not auto-normalize P1→must at the spec render/gate stage?
clarifications.a: Alpha policy prohibits backward-compatibility layers. A normalization layer adds complexity for a problem solvable at the source.

clarifications.q: Why not relax the spec.json schema to accept P1/P2/P3?
clarifications.a: Would allow two representations to coexist, causing inconsistency in rendered output and downstream tools.

alternatives_considered.option: B: Auto-normalize P1→must at spec render/gate
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected — adds conversion layer, alpha policy prohibits backward-compatibility code.

alternatives_considered.option: D: Relax spec.json schema to accept P1/P2/P3
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected — two notations coexist, no single source of truth.
